### Assistant Professor of Biostatistics, Emory University

<br><img src="images/headshots/hs1.jpg" alt="julia" style="width:30%"><br>


I am an Assistant Professor in the [Department of Biostatistics and Bioinformatics](https://sph.emory.edu/departments/bios/index.html) at Emory University, a Fellow of the [Emory Center for AI Learning](https://ailearning.emory.edu/), and Director of the [Biostatistics, Epidemiology, and Research Design (BERD) program](https://georgiactsa.org/research/berd/index.html) for the Georgia Clinical and Translational Science Alliance. Prior to joining Emory in 2023, I held a faculty appointment at the [Colorado School of Public Health](https://coloradosph.cuanschutz.edu/). I received my PhD in Biostatistics from [Columbia University](https://www.mailman.columbia.edu/become-student/departments/biostatistics) in 2019 and my BA in Chemistry from [Swarthmore College](https://www.swarthmore.edu/) in 2010.

My research focuses on developing statistical methods and computational tools for complex biomedical data, with particular emphasis on functional data analysis. My work spans digital health and wearable technologies, biomedical imaging, and spatial biology, and is motivated by methodological challenges arising from interdisciplinary biomedical research. I also develop open-source statistical software to make these methods accessible to the broader research community and facilitate reproducibility.
